why: All three checks confirm the finding. (1) Quote is verbatim: features-overview.md line 193 reads '* **Skills and subagents** override by name: when the same name exists at multiple levels, one definition wins based on priority (managed > user > project for skills; managed > CLI flag > project > user > plugin for subagents).' The rest of that line ('Plugin skills are namespaced to avoid conflicts. See skill discovery and subagent scope.') does not reverse it, and skills.md:122 corroborates independently: 'When skills share the same name across levels, enterprise overrides personal, and personal overrides project. A skill at any of these levels also overrides a bundled skill with the same name.' (2) The cited code says what was claimed: packages/shared/src/capabilities/resolver.ts:863-869 scopeSpecificity returns project 3 / workspace 2 / global 1 / builtin 0, and applyCollisionPolicy (:2011, preference tuple :2038-2042, sort :2045-2051) sorts every non-MCP bucket -- skills included, bucket key is `${kind}\u0000${logicalName}` at :2017 -- by scopeSpecificity DESCENDING, so the project record wins the unqualified alias. The docblock at :1993-2010 cites mcp.md for the MCP arm only; no skills.md citation exists for the non-MCP arm, and no test covers the user-vs-project pair (resolver.test.ts:255-263 covers workspace-vs-plugin, :266-283 covers same-scope nessy-vs-portable). (3) The consequence is real, verified empirically and one layer down, not inferred. A throwaway probe test through createCapabilityResolver with two same-named skill records -- scope global and scope project -- returned: global key alias=false, project key alias=true. The alias is load-bearing downstream: base-agent.ts:2124-2126 builds skillsByAlias from `runtime.view.skills.filter(skill => skill.selectedAsUnqualifiedAlias)`, and :2345-2350 gates bare-name skill mention resolution on the same flag, so a bare `deploy` reference resolves to the project skill and the user's own is reachable only by its qualified key. Scope mapping is unambiguous: native-sources.ts:899-904 puts BOTH `~/.agents/skills` (portable, the direct analogue of `~/.claude/skills`) and `${CONFIG_DIR}/skills` (CONFIG_DIR = `~/.nessy-agent`, paths.ts:18-21) at scope 'global', while :996-1010 puts `<project>/.nessy-agent/skills` at scope 'project'. Not an owner decision: none of the nine dated decisions in 2026-07-29-inert-worklist.md section 3 concerns scope precedence (they are SEATBELT_TESTING_WILDCARD, availableModels, autoMode.classifyAllShell, ManagedDeliveryStateV1.drops, hooks-runtime.ts, SdkMcpServerConfig.required, and three SessionMirrorStore rows), and grepping the plans and the parity audit for a skill-precedence ruling returns nothing. Not a deliberate fork difference either: this is neither a subscription-flow drop, a gateway concern, nor a rename. The one refinement to the claim's wording: the losing record is not removed -- it stays enabled and addressable by qualified key, and an info-severity diagnostic capability.collision.unqualified-alias is emitted (:2055-2061) -- but the bare name, which is what a user or the model types, does go to the project definition, which is the inversion the doc forbids.
correctedState: Confirmed with one wording refinement. Skill name collisions across scopes are resolved by scopeSpecificity (resolver.ts:863-869) inside applyCollisionPolicy (:2011-2062), which ranks project(3) > workspace(2) > global(1) > builtin(0) for every non-MCP kind including skills. Measured through createCapabilityResolver: with a same-named skill at scope 'global' (`~/.agents/skills` and `~/.nessy-agent/skills`) and at scope 'project' (`<project>/.nessy-agent/skills`), the PROJECT record gets selectedAsUnqualifiedAlias=true and the global one false -- the inverse of Claude's documented 'personal overrides project' (skills.md:122). Since base-agent.ts:2124-2126 and :2345-2350 resolve bare-name skill references only through the alias winner, a repo that checks in `.nessy-agent/skills/deploy` takes over the bare name `deploy` from the user's own skill. The user's skill is NOT deleted -- it stays enabled, addressable by its qualified capability key, and an info-severity `capability.collision.unqualified-alias` diagnostic is recorded -- but the bare name goes the wrong way. The builtin arm matches the doc (any scope beats bundled); only the user-vs-project pair is inverted, and 'workspace' has no Claude counterpart. The docblock at :1993-2010 cites mcp.md for the MCP arm alone and no test exercises the user-vs-project pair, so the skill arm was never checked against skills.md.
